problem: A particle moves from the origin with an acceleration of $(-2i+j)\,{\text{ft/s}}^{2}$ and an initial velocity of $(4i+j)\,\text{ft/s}.$ Find the distance from the particle to the origin after $4$ seconds.

feedback.problem: A particle moves from the origin with an acceleration of $(2i-4j)\,{\text{in/s}}^{2}$ and an initial velocity of $(i-2j)\,\text{in/s}.$ Find the position vector of the particle after $3$ seconds.
feedback.worked_solution:
If a particle moves with constant acceleration $a,$ the position vector of the particle at time $t$ can be found using

$$
r={r}_{0}+ut+\frac{1}{2}a{t}^{2},
$$

 

where ${r}_{0}$ is the initial position of the particle and $u$ is its initial velocity.

In our case, we have

$$
{r}_{0}=0i+0j,\,u=i-2j,\,a=2i-4j.
$$

Therefore, the position vector of the particle after $t=3\,\text{s}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =(0i+0j)+(i-2j)(3)+\frac{1}{2}(2i-4j)(3)^{2} \\  & =(3i-6j)+9(i-2j) \\  & =(3i-6j)+(9i-18j) \\  & =(12i-24j)\,\text{in}.\end{aligned}
$$
